AiNET's own homepage, successfully reached this session after an earlier certificate error had blocked access, describes the company as operating in the Washington DC and Baltimore corridor and references its CyberNAP service, already on file elsewhere in this registry under a separate Glen Burnie, Maryland row, but the homepage gives no facility specific detail for a One Market Center location in Baltimore, and no square footage or power capacity was found published for this building. This Baltimore location appears to be a smaller or more specialized site within AiNET's regional network, consistent with the One Market Center name referencing a specific downtown Baltimore office or interconnection building rather than a large standalone data center campus, though this session could not independently confirm that characterization. No square footage or MW figure could be confirmed for this specific building this session despite a fresh attempt, an honest gap rather than a fabricated estimate.

reading.body:
AiNET One Market Center sits at 300 West Lexington Street in Baltimore's downtown, positioned within a regional operator that claims 400+ MW of total capacity across its network but publishes no specific figure for this location. The operator's publicly available materials describe it as part of the Washington DC and Baltimore corridor, consistent with AiNET's larger CyberNAP facility near Fort Meade, but AiNET does not publish square footage, power capacity, or technical specifications for the One Market Center site itself.

Without published capacity, this campus cannot be ranked against others by power draw. Maryland has 11 mapped data center facilities on file, but only three publish power figures, totaling 9.3 MW of disclosed capacity statewide; this facility contributes zero to that published total and therefore ranks fourth among Maryland's mapped sites by a metric that cannot be measured from public sources.

Whether One Market Center matters to AI scaling depends on information AiNET has chosen not to disclose. The name suggests a specialized interconnection or colocation point rather than a large standalone campus, but this reading cannot move beyond that inference without published specifications.
